question: If so, what controls, sampling/testing requirements, or documentation requirements currently apply?

Build 01.answer:
## 1. Short answer

**If the consignment’s product description and CN code fall within the current Annex II listing for dried figs from Türkiye in Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, special import conditions apply.** These generally include official controls at the relevant EU border control post, advance notification and a CHED-D, plus an official certificate and sampling-and-analysis results from the competent authority in the country of origin.

The listing and its control frequency can change. Confirm the applicable entry against the consolidated legislation in force on the date of import.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Regulation (EU) 2019/1793** sets temporary increased official controls and special import conditions for certain foods from specified countries. For goods listed in **Annex II**, the special conditions include an official certificate and results of sampling and analysis. The exact requirements depend on the current Annex entry and whether the consignment’s product and CN code are covered.
- Official controls on entry are conducted under **Regulation (EU) 2017/625**. For covered consignments, the importer or responsible operator must make the required advance notification through the relevant EU system and submit a **CHED-D**. The consignment must be presented at an appropriate border control post.
- The official-check frequency in the applicable Annex entry determines how often identity and physical checks, including sampling, are carried out. It does **not** necessarily mean every consignment is sampled. Documentary checks and any required origin-country certificate and analysis results are separate requirements.
- Official sampling and analysis for mycotoxins are governed by **Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782**. The aflatoxin results must also be assessed against the applicable maximum levels in **Regulation (EU) 2023/915**.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

- Verify the **current Annex II entry**, CN codes, named aflatoxins and prescribed control frequency for the particular dried-fig product and import date. Do not assume the requirements apply to every fig product or preparation.
- Check the current certificate model, the required scope of the accompanying analysis results, the notification timing and the designated border control post. These details depend on the applicable entry and current implementing rules.
- The fact that aflatoxin B1 was detected does not, by itself, establish that the consignment exceeds the applicable legal maximum or determine its import outcome. That requires the relevant product category, valid sampling and analysis, and the applicable limits.

## 1. Short answer

The supplied evidence supports a **conditional** answer: if this dried-fig consignment falls within the relevant entries in Annex I or II of Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, the sampling and analysis for aflatoxins must follow Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782. The evidence provided does **not** establish whether dried figs from Türkiye are currently listed, what control frequency or sampling rate applies, or which documents this particular consignment must carry.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Article 3, specifies that sampling and analyses for food listed in its Annexes I and II because of possible mycotoxin contamination, including aflatoxins, must be performed in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2023/2782. The provision concerns competent-authority checks at border control posts or control points and, where the regulation requires results to accompany consignments, analyses performed in third countries. **The condition that the food is listed in the relevant Annex must first be verified.** [E4]
- For official controls and other official activities, Regulation (EU) 2017/625, Article 34, requires applicable Union sampling or analytical methods to be followed. It also requires samples to be taken, handled and labelled so their legal, scientific and technical validity is ensured. [E1][E2]
- The cited Article 3 refers to analytical results accompanying consignments **where those results are required by the regulation**; it does not establish from the evidence supplied that such results, a particular certificate, or any other specified document are required for this shipment. The general certification provision cited in Article 86 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 does not identify the documents applicable to these figs. [E4][E5]

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

Verify the current Annex entry for dried figs originating in Türkiye, including any applicable conditions, control frequency, sampling rate, and required accompanying documents. The supplied excerpts do not establish those details or whether the detected aflatoxin B1 makes the shipment non-compliant: that also requires the applicable maximum level and a legally valid analytical result.

Build 03-B.answer:
## 1. Short answer

On the evidence available, **dried figs originating in Türkiye fall within Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2019/1793**, for aflatoxins and ochratoxin A. The listed frequency of identity and physical checks is **30%**. That is a control frequency for the listed product entry—not a guarantee that a particular consignment will or will not be tested.

For a consignment within that Annex II entry, the rules require **third-country sampling and analysis results and an official certificate**, as well as prior notification and a completed CHED for entry and release. EU sampling and analysis for mycotoxins must follow the method rules referenced in Regulation 2019/1793. The known detection does not, by itself, establish whether this consignment is legally non-compliant: that depends on the result, the applicable product classification and the relevant maximum level.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Import controls:** Regulation 2019/1793, Annex II, Section 1, row 14, lists Türkiye-origin dried figs for aflatoxins and ochratoxin A, with a **30% frequency** of identity and physical checks. Article 8 says those checks include sampling and laboratory analysis, at the Annex frequency. The listed product scope and CN/TARIC classification must match the actual goods.
- **Sampling and testing:** Article 3(a) directs sampling and analysis of foods listed for mycotoxin risks, including aflatoxins, to **Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782**. Article 10 requires each Annex II consignment to be accompanied by sampling and analysis results from the competent authority in Türkiye (or, if different, the country of consignment); the results must identify the consignment. The analyses must be performed by laboratories accredited to **ISO/IEC 17025**.
- **Documents and identification:** Under Articles 9–11, the consignment must have an identification code, shown on each individual bag or packaging form (subject to the stated exception for combined packaging); the analysis results must bear that code; and the consignment must be accompanied by the prescribed official certificate. The certificate is issued by the relevant third-country competent authority and presented at the border control post.
- **Notification and entry document:** Regulation 2017/625, Article 56, requires the operator responsible for the consignment to submit the relevant CHED information through IMSOC for prior notification. Regulation 2019/1013 generally sets prior notification at least **one working day** before expected arrival, with a possible shorter period of at least four hours where logistical constraints prevent meeting that deadline. Regulation 2019/1793, Article 4, requires a duly finalised CHED before customs release for free circulation.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

The listed 30% frequency does not establish whether this particular shipment has been selected, sampled, or already tested at the EU border. Nor does the fact that aflatoxin B1 was detected establish a breach without the result, sampling basis and applicable product classification. If the sample indicates a result above the applicable legal maximum, the authority would need to assess compliance and decide the consignment’s disposition; the facts supplied do not establish that outcome.

Cellar metadata observed on **19 October 2026** identifies 30 June 2026 as the latest observed consolidation candidate for Regulation 2019/1793 and 19 August 2026 for Regulation 2023/915. That is a metadata observation, **not verification of article-level law, application dates or all transitional rules**. Before acting, check the current Annex II entry, the exact CN/TARIC classification, any amendments and their entry-into-force or application dates, and the current text of Regulation 2023/2782 for the precise sampling procedure.

Direct answer
- The supplied Annex II snapshot lists dried figs from Türkiye under CN code 0804 20 90. If that is the shipment’s correct classification, the consignment falls within the Annex II listing. (Regulation 2019/1793, ANNEX II / table 2 / HTML row 135 / entry 14 [Ec3c379af9bf38771])
  Condition: The product must be correctly classified under CN code 0804 20 90.

Legal requirements
- Consignments listed in Annex II are subject to official controls at border control posts on entry into the Union and at control points. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 7 [Eb5778b93a88ed5c1])
  Condition: Applies if the consignment is covered by the Annex II listing, including the relevant CN/TARIC classification.
- For Annex II-listed consignments, the competent authorities carry out identity and physical checks, including sampling and laboratory analyses, at the frequency specified in Annex II. The supplied dried-fig row does not state a check frequency, and the available records do not establish that the 30% frequency shown for other CN codes applies to dried figs. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 8 [E37470f1e9ecea27c]; Regulation 2019/1793, ANNEX II / table 2 / HTML row 135 / entry 14 [Ec3c379af9bf38771])
  Condition: The frequency must be established from the applicable Annex II entry; it cannot be inferred from another row in the same country listing.
- Each Annex II consignment must be accompanied by results of sampling and analyses performed on that consignment by the competent authority of the country of origin or, if different, the country of consignment. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 10 [Ef1fe4fee24b0bc76])
  Condition: Applies if the goods are covered by Annex II.
- The accompanying analyses must be performed by laboratories accredited to ISO/IEC 17025. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 10 [Ef1fe4fee24b0bc76])
  Condition: Applies to the analyses referred to in Article 10(1) for Annex II consignments.
- A duly finalised CHED is required before customs may allow release for free circulation of consignments listed in Annex I or Annex II. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 4 [E44dfdc757d2df2aa])
  Condition: Applies if the consignment is listed in Annex I or Annex II.
- Each Annex II consignment must carry an identification code; ordinarily, each individual bag or other packaging form must carry that code too. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 9 [Ec369db707437897c])
  Condition: If one outer bag or packaging combines several small packages, the code on that outer packaging is sufficient.
- For food listed in Annex I or II because of possible mycotoxin contamination, including aflatoxins, official sampling and analyses must follow Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782. (Regulation 2019/1793, Article 3 [E5c089437f3b0191e])

Article 36
Sampling of animals and goods offered for sale by means of distance communication
1. In the case of animals and goods offered for sale by means of distance communication, samples ordered from operators by the competent authorities without identifying themselves may be used for the purposes of an official control.
2. Competent authorities, once they are in possession of the samples, shall take all steps to ensure that the operators from whom these samples have been ordered in accordance with paragraph 1: (a) are informed that such samples have been taken in the context of an official control and, where appropriate, are analysed or tested for the purposes of such official control; and (b) where the samples referred to in that paragraph are analysed or tested, are able to exercise the right to a second expert opinion, as provided for in Article 35(1).
3. Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall apply to delegated bodies and natural persons to which certain official controls tasks have been delegated.

evidence.location: Article 61a
evidence.text:
Article 61a
Fact-finding missions
Commission experts shall perform fact-finding missions in Member States to assess the application, by laboratories and by other testing facilities, of the relevant standards for carrying out tests and studies submitted to the Authority as part of an application, as well as compliance with the notification obligation set out in Article 32b(3), by 28 March 2025. By that date, Commission experts shall also perform fact-finding missions to assess the application of those standards by laboratories and other testing facilities located in third countries insofar as set out in relevant agreements and arrangements with those third countries, including as referred to in Article 49.
Non-compliance identified during those fact-finding missions shall be brought to the attention of the Commission, Member States, the Authority as well as the assessed laboratories and other testing facilities. The Commission, the Authority and Member States shall ensure the appropriate follow-up to such identified non-compliance.
The outcome of these fact-finding missions shall be presented in an overview report. On the basis of that report, the Commission shall submit a legislative proposal, if appropriate, as regards, in particular, any necessary control procedures, including audits.

evidence.location: Article 1
evidence.text:
Article 1
Prior notification of consignments
1. The operator responsible for a consignment falling within the categories of animals and goods referred to in Article 47(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 shall give prior notification, to the competent authority of the border control post of first arrival into the Union, at least one working day before the expected arrival of the consignment.
2. By way of derogation from paragraph 1, where logistical constraints prevent compliance with the time limit set out in that paragraph, the competent authorities of the border control posts may apply a period of prior notification of at least four hours before the expected arrival of the consignment.
3. By way of derogation from paragraph 1, the competent authorities of border control posts designated for imports of unprocessed logs and sawn and chipped wood in accordance with Article 4 of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/1012 may apply a period of prior notification of up to five working days before the expected arrival of such consignments.
